external_invariants: Goal and metric scope (request.json): reduce latency for one complete offline batch=32 image inference, preserving the source quality checks; the objective is latency_ms (unit ms, direction minimize) with no objective-level constraints; the workload remains offline batch=32 with goals throughput (images_per_second, max) and memory (peak_allocated_bytes, min).

Model is pretrained ResNet-18 loaded from the local assets via ResNetForImageClassification.from_pretrained(assets, local_files_only=True, dtype=torch.float32) with eval() behavior; weights and activations stay FP32.

Numerical policies preserved from common.py:34-42: torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'), torch.manual_seed(20261020), 4 CPU threads and 1 interop thread.

Input is the offline batch of 32: images = np.load(assets/pixels.npy) moved to CUDA (shape (3,3,224,224) float32), pixels = images[torch.arange(32, device='cuda') % 3].contiguous() -> (32,3,224,224) FP32, GPU-resident before the timed boundary; no H2D transfer or preprocessing inside run().
The measured workload is exactly one model(pixel_values=pixels).logits forward under torch.inference_mode(); no reduction of the work amount, batch, image size or class dimension.

Correctness requires the full 1000-class logits compared with atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4 (torch.testing.assert_close) and exact top-1 equality torch.equal(actual.argmax(-1), reference.argmax(-1)); the +1-corruption negative control must be rejected.

latency_ms is the wall-clock latency of exactly one complete offline forward on the batch of 32 under the source's per-repeat protocol (resnet_inference.py:42-48): torch.cuda.synchronize, torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats, time.perf_counter_ns around one infer(), synchronize; the framework reproduces this by synchronizing at both boundaries of run(); samples summarize to median/min/max; it must not be converted into a cached-only, partial or unsynchronized latency.

images_per_second is the source's full-request throughput for the fixed batch of 32, computed as batch * 1e3 / latency_ms around one complete forward on the GPU-resident input; it must not be converted into a cached-only throughput.

peak_allocated_bytes is the process-level PyTorch CUDA allocated peak for one forward with peak stats reset immediately before the timed call (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated after the synchronized run), not whole-device, reserved or driver memory.

Goal constraints (request.json): the latency_ms objective carries no constraints; the memory workload goal (min peak_allocated_bytes) retains the constraint images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio = 0.95, i.e. images_per_second >= 0.95 * baseline; latency reduction must not be obtained by violating this ratio or the frozen workload/precision/data.
Model loading, weight transfer to GPU and input construction happen in prepare outside timed execution; the module creates no CUDA tensors and initializes no CUDA context at import time.
